# Arrays are named for the CUDA kernel's own parameters, IN LOWER CASE: a name in this
# format is [a-z0-9_], so `I`, `K`, `E`, `R` and `C` are written `i`, `k`, `e`, `r` and `c`.
# Every f32 token is the little-endian bit pattern of the value; a bf16 operand is recorded
# as the f32 its sixteen bits widen to, so the Metal side loads the same bits after narrowing.
# A scalar is an array of length 1.
#
# C = 20 channels, K = 4 taps, R = 3 requests in slots {2, 0, 1} of a 3-slot pool.
#
# conv_update        <- pie::ssm::causal_conv1d_update_batched<bf16>(x, weight, bias=null, state_base, slot_ids, slot_stride_elems=80, y, R=3, C=20, K=4)
#                       grid [ceil(C/256), R] x 256 -- ssm.rs::causal_conv1d
# conv_chunked       <- pie::ssm::causal_conv1d_prefill_batched<bf16>(x, weight, bias=null, y, state_out_base, slot_ids, qo_indptr, slot_stride_elems=80, C=20, K=4, write_state=true, mask=null, commit_len=null)
#                       grid [C, R] x 64 -- ssm.rs::causal_conv1d_chunked below its R >= 8 channel-tile arm
#                       qo_indptr = {0, 3, 9, 14}: one window SHORTER than K, so the trailing-state write reads taps back off the slab
# conv_chunked_empty <- the same kernel at qo_indptr = {0, 0, 4, 9}: request 0's window is empty and both sides return early
#
# THE SLAB IS [num_slots, K, C], oldest tap at row 0, C the fast axis -- the same rectangle on
# both sides. CUDA holds it in bf16 and causal_conv1d.metal in float, so every value here is
# bf16-exact and the two planes hold one number. CUDA shifts the slab in place and Metal writes
# a second plane, so `conv_state` is the slab as launched and `new_conv_state` is the slab as it
# came back. THE METAL SIDE MUST SEED new_conv_state WITH conv_state BEFORE DISPATCHING -- that is
# what Pool::carry_forward leaves behind, and conv_chunked_empty is the case that depends on it.
# `bias` is null: the Metal kernels have no such operand and both Rust claim bodies pass none.
